question: Should Discord Activity support be rebuilt under the Canvas/Discord plugin contracts with a fail-closed Activity auth model, continued through the newer overlapping branch after repair, or paused?
rationale: The remaining choice crosses plugin ownership, Gateway authorization, token transport, operator config shape, and two overlapping dirty branches, so automation can identify defects but should not choose the permanent Activity security boundary.

options.title: Rebuild under plugin auth
options.body: Move the Activity config, routing, and A2UI bridge into Canvas/Discord plugin contracts, require explicit credentials, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof before merge.

options.title: Continue through newer PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/65205 only after its similar security, compatibility, proof, and merge-state blockers are resolved.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Keep this as design context and defer Discord Activities until maintainers settle whether the security model belongs in Canvas, Discord, or an external package.

recommendation.title: Rebuild under plugin auth
recommendation.body: Move the Activity config, routing, and A2UI bridge into Canvas/Discord plugin contracts, require explicit credentials, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The hardest decision is the Gateway auth and Canvas plugin ownership boundary introduced by recent Canvas plugin-surface work.
